---
title: 'Release candidates'
description: 'Pin a main commit as a release candidate so its full required CI set finishes while main keeps moving, without a main merge freeze.'
updatedAt: '2026-11-24'
audience: developers
---

A production release needs one main commit with its whole required CI set
green. Main moves every few minutes, and several always-on workflows coalesce
main pushes into one shared pending run, so a newer push supersedes the pending
run of the previous commit. Before release candidates, a release round needed
a main merge freeze to get one green commit. A release candidate removes the
freeze: the production owner pins a commit, and its runs live on their own ref
where no main push can cancel them.

## What gets pinned

`scripts/ci/release-candidate-core.mjs` owns the set:

| Group | Workflows | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dispatched on the candidate ref | Codex Plugin, Docs/SEO, i18n, MFA contract, Security Checks | Main pushes share one `latest` concurrency group, so a later push drops the pending run. |
| Dispatched on the candidate ref | Cron Control producer | It is path-filtered, so most commits have no producer run. Dispatch ignores path filters. |
| Dispatched on the candidate ref | Test, Type Check | A newer main push cancels the older run ([main-push supersession](/build/devops/github-actions-runbook#main-push-supersession)). |
| Observed from the main push | Oxc | Each main SHA keeps its own non-cancelling group. |

`scripts/ci/release-candidate.test.mjs` fails when a new always-on main
workflow uses a shared main group but is missing from the dispatched list, or
when an observed workflow loses its per-SHA group.

A dispatched Security Checks run uses its `workflow_dispatch` mode, so it also
runs CodeQL and the findings register. The register fails while confirmed
critical or high findings are open, which is a release blocker anyway.

## Procedure (production owner)

1. Pick a commit on main and nominate it:

   ```bash
   gh workflow run release-candidate.yaml -R tutur3u/platform -f sha=<40-hex sha>
   ```

   The job checks that the SHA is in main. It then creates
   `release-candidate/<sha>` and dispatches each dispatched workflow that has
   no candidate run yet. Nominating the same SHA again only fills gaps.
2. Watch the result in **Admin → Deployments → Release candidates**, in
   `gh run list -R tutur3u/platform --commit <sha>`, or with a status pass:

   ```bash
   gh workflow run release-candidate.yaml -R tutur3u/platform -f sha=<sha> -f mode=status
   ```

   A status pass writes the required-set table to the job summary. It reruns
   each cancelled run once. A rerun takes a unique concurrency group, so it
   cannot be superseded. It also dispatches any dispatched workflow that is
   missing and has no candidate run. It fails only when a required workflow is
   red. Pending is not an error.
3. When the verdict is green, promote with the pinned-SHA `bun git-sync` path
   as usual. A release candidate never deploys. Who may deploy, the production
   workflows and their gates stay unchanged.

Keep merging to main throughout; nothing waits for the candidate. A
candidate ref protects its runs until it is pruned: a pass keeps the newest
three candidates and drops any older than seven days.

## Evidence rule

A run counts for the candidate SHA only when it ran in `tutur3u/platform` at
exactly that SHA and is one of these:

- a `push` on `main`;
- a `workflow_dispatch` on `release-candidate/<that sha>`.

A green run of a workflow outranks newer cancelled or red runs of the same
workflow. The verdict is green only when every required workflow is green; a
required workflow with no evidence counts as pending. The Admin panel applies
the same rule and the same list, and
`scripts/ci/release-candidate.test.mjs` keeps the two lists equal. The panel
scans at most five candidate refs (six GitHub calls) and shows the newest three
by run time.

<Warning>
Artifact provenance gates are unchanged. The Cron Control `already serving`
verifier and the production owner's local Cron driver still accept only a
producer run with `event == push` on `head_branch == main`. A candidate Cron
producer is build evidence for the SHA. It is not an approved artifact source
until a reviewed change accepts `workflow_dispatch` on
`release-candidate/<sha>` with a main-ancestry check.
</Warning>

## Bounds and cost

- Only the release-candidate workflow on `main` acts. It uses a five-minute job
  with `actions: write` and `contents: write`. GitHub cannot scope these
  permissions to one ref, so the job keeps its attack surface small instead:
  - it checks out only the two scripts at `github.workflow_sha`;
  - it uses SHA-pinned first-party actions and no installed dependencies;
  - it passes the inputs through the environment, never into a shell
    expression;
  - it validates the SHA before any call;
  - it writes only `refs/heads/release-candidate/<40-hex sha>`, dispatches
    only the fixed workflow list, and reruns only runs of the required set.
- At most two other candidates may have runs in progress when a nomination
  starts; otherwise it is refused (`CANDIDATE_LIMIT`).
- A pass inspects at most eight candidate refs. More than that means refs were
  created by hand, and the pass refuses before any per-candidate call
  (`CANDIDATE_REF_LIMIT`). Delete the stray refs, then nominate again.
- Each nomination prunes candidate refs beyond the newest three, and any ref
  older than seven days. Refs that do not match `release-candidate/<own sha>`
  are never touched.
- One nomination costs about six workflow runs. Ordinary main pushes cost
  nothing extra.

## Why not a merge queue or concurrency changes

- **Merge queue.** A merge queue needs pull requests and a `merge_group`
  trigger on every required workflow. It also serializes every lane, which
  conflicts with the direct-to-main flow.
- **Per-SHA groups on every main push.** These would drop the coalescing that
  keeps queue pressure under the Free plan's concurrent-job cap.
- **Pin-aware concurrency keys.** The pin is chosen after the push, so a key
  computed at push time cannot know about it.

## Failure handling

- `CANDIDATE_NOT_IN_MAIN`: the SHA is not an ancestor of main. Pick a main commit.
- `CANDIDATE_LIMIT`: wait for an active candidate to finish, or let pruning remove old ones.
- `CANDIDATE_GITHUB … POST /git/refs -> 403/422`: a ruleset blocked the token
  from creating the ref. Create `release-candidate/<sha>` with your own
  credentials, then nominate again. The job keeps an existing ref.
- A red required workflow: fix forward on main and nominate the new commit, or
  rerun a flaky job by hand.
